article_title: The Price of Finding a Certificate: Unsupported Pareto Points under Prefix Queries
article_abstract: We study the cost of discovering a certificate for a designated candidate whose two objectives are means of ordered vector records. Each query purchases the next whole record of one configuration. Algorithms must decide correctly on every legal archive, and their acquisition cost on positive archives is compared with the cheapest realised prefix proving both Pareto nondomination and unsupportedness under nonzero nonnegative weights. This is a geometric instance-complexity problem with mandatory predecessor payments. When the cost coordinate is unbounded, we determine the exact deterministic and zero-error randomised ratios for every catalogue size and archive length. The randomised lower bound covers numerical policies and arbitrary prefix interleavings through a causal Ramsey reduction. Bounded diagonal bands yield sharp three-configuration transitions under positive row prices. For three configurations on the triangle, a uniform policy has ratio at most 12/11. A matching asymptotic lower bound determines the exact limiting ratio of policies that fully observe the candidate before TRUE. Approaching the unrestricted asymptotic lower bound 23/22 instead requires partial candidate observation on the exhibited hard family. A certificate-preservation criterion characterises transcript-preserving policy transfer, and public constant blocks yield sharp comparator-distortion bounds. The unrestricted triangle optimum remains open.
